Besides, the `i386-linux-generic` doesn't see a valid triple?

Doesn't matter what clang errors on, the IR is the IR and should work

Doesn't matter, it asserts

comments.author: phoebewang
comments.body: The point is the IR is not valid. The `half`/`bfloat` type support requires SSE2 instructions, so we limit it to SSE2 in FE. IR has more flexibility and can represent more invalid combination to the backend. I don't think we need to handle the exhaustless invalid cases.

comments.author: arsenm
comments.body:
> The point is the IR is not valid. The `half`/`bfloat` type support requires SSE2 instructions, so we limit it to SSE2 in FE. 

The IR is valid. What clang bothers to support has no bearing on the validity of the IR. You can always handle this in some way, by bitcasting to i16 or whatever you want. You can invent whatever ABI you want for the IR. 

> IR has more flexibility and can represent more invalid combination to the backend. I don't think we need to handle the exhaustless invalid cases.

This is an extremely poor QoI, and restricts the ability to share tests. I ran into this trying to add tests that had 32-bit run lines, and now I have to work around backend bugs.  Asserting on IR that passes the verifier is never acceptable
